CM is inside ∠ACB, representing the angle bisector of ∠ACB; CN is inside ∠DCE, representing the angle bisector of ∠DCE. Reasoning: Given ∠ACB = 45°, CM bisects ∠ACB, so ∠BCM = 45° ÷ 2 = 22.5°. Given ∠DCE = 60°, CN bisects ∠DCE, so ∠DCN = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°. Because CB and CD are opposite rays on the same straight line, from CB to CD forms a straight angle of 180°. Therefore ∠MCN = 180° − ∠BCM − ∠DCN = 180° − 22.5° − 30° = 127.5°.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: B, C, and D are drawn on one straight horizontal line, with ray CA above the left side of the line and ray CE above the right side; CM is the internal bisector ray of angle ACB and CN is the internal bisector ray of angle DCE. From the text, use ∠ACB = 45° and ∠DCE = 60°. Since CM bisects ∠ACB, ∠BCM = 22.5°. Since CN bisects ∠DCE, ∠DCN = 30°. Because CB and CD are opposite rays on the same straight line, the straight angle from CB to CD is 180°, so ∠MCN = 180° − 22.5° − 30° = 127.5°.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: take the straight line B-C-D as a baseline, with CD pointing to the right and CB pointing to the left; CA lies above-left from C and CE lies above-right from C. From the text, ∠ACB = 45° and ∠DCE = 60°, and CM and CN are their internal bisectors. Assign directions measured counterclockwise from ray CD: CD has direction 0° and CB has direction 180°. Since CE makes 60° with CD, CN, the bisector of ∠DCE, has direction 30°. Since CA is 45° away from CB toward CD, CA has direction 180° − 45° = 135°, so CM, the bisector between CB at 180° and CA at 135°, has direction (180° + 135°)/2 = 157.5°. The angle between rays CM and CN is 157.5° − 30° = 127.5°.
